steps.what: Observe food service operations against nutritional, safety, sanitation and quality standards
Resolve nutritional and safety deviations with food service personnel

tasks.design: Keep direct monitoring and corrective decisions with the dietitian. Existing {DOCS} standards support the inspection; no sensor coverage or separate reporting burden is invented.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conformance depends on observing actual food handling and nutritional practice.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated replacement for this monitoring activity.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe practice and deciding immediate corrections.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret conditions on site and hold a useful corrective conversation.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Direct operational observation and corrective judgement retain their time in this proposed design.

assumptions: Boundary is dietitian oversight, excluding food-service staff corrections and the separate individual meal inspection task; roll-ups resolve overlap.
Dietitian produces observed deviations in s1, with observation time fully counted. No structured conformance feed is assumed.
Review native checklists before new software. No changed tool or service means zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which conditions require direct observation rather than existing records?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65+35=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Observing service practice and resolving deviations retain their full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect meals for prescribed diet conformance, palatability and appearance

tasks.design: Retain inspection of the actual served meal and its suitability. The {DOCS} prescribed diet is a reference, and a recipe record does not prove what was served or how it tastes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appearance, palatability and actual substitutions require direct assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: No relevant validated meal inspection capability is established in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting incorrect portions or ingredients and judging acceptability.
tasks.human_edge: Combine sensory assessment with knowledge of the prescribed diet.
tasks.altitude: Meal inspection and correction authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Escalate deviations from the prescribed diet

evidence.claim: A digital menu is insufficient evidence of actual meal conformance or palatability; no inspection saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is dietitian inspection of served meals, excluding preparation and corrections by kitchen staff.
The treating care process produces the prescribed diet; its clinical production is unchanged and not claimed as free structured input to automation. This task contains no machine action.
Use existing reference access first. Unchanged sensory inspection requires zero new upkeep.
research_questions: Which errors are visible only in the served meal?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. The complete physical and sensory inspection remains human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Purchase food meeting health and safety requirements

steps.what: Specify food quantities and check supplier health and safety suitability
Assemble food purchase lines from the verified brief
Confirm compliant purchase lines and place the food order

tasks.design: Configure {PROCUREMENT} to populate order lines only from the dietitian's verified purchase brief. Health and safety suitability, substitutions and supplier selection remain human decisions before the exact order is placed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated purchase-line entry follows a separate suitability assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Native requisition templates can copy verified fields without making food safety judgements.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier substitutions and incomplete or stale specifications.
tasks.human_edge: Judge suitability and refuse unsafe substitutions.
tasks.altitude: Less order entry, with unchanged purchase approval responsibility.

reach.task: Reconcile food deliveries with dietary requirements

evidence.claim: Copying verified purchase fields into draft orders is a plausible native procurement configuration; the digest gives no food-purchasing case or measured saving.

assumptions: Boundary is dietitian purchase specification, entry and placement, excluding receiving, supplier production and payment.

Dietitian produces item code, approved specification version, supplier, quantity, unit, price, delivery date and location in s1. Its full 40 hours include capture and missing-field clarification; s2 never infers compliant status from absence of a warning.
Test native templates first. Missing or changed specifications stop line population and return to manual entry and assessment.
Five additional focal hours cover catalogue checks, template maintenance and failed order handling; two other-role hours cover procurement mappings.
unknowns: How much purchase time is duplicate entry
research_questions: Can verified brief fields populate orders without increasing capture or review time?

already_counted.description: Food suitability checks and purchase brief capture
Final line review and order placement

incremental.description: Catalogue audits, template upkeep and order exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact supplier, item and specification versions, quantities, prices and delivery details; any substitution voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+0+30=70, gross=30, focal upkeep=5, net=25. High assumes the 30-hour entry component is genuinely duplicated and the verified brief already captures all fields; low retains manual entry when specifications vary plus upkeep. No safety assessment saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop food service and nutrition policies

steps.what: Define nutritional program policy aims and review supporting evidence
Develop draft food service or nutritional program policy text

loop.output: Draft clauses with source references and unresolved choices
loop.check: Dietitian checks clinical meaning, source support, implementation feasibility and conflicts between clauses
loop.stop: One draft; unsupported claims or unresolved obligations return to manual policy development
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy explanation and synthesis need contextual wording beyond fixed clauses

steps.what: Evaluate policy tradeoffs and submit the final recommendation

tasks.design: Draft referenced clauses in {DOCS} from a dietitian-selected evidence pack. Retain policy aims, clinical tradeoffs and final recommendation with the dietitian; formal organisational adoption remains outside this authoring boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated policy wording competes with evidence review and practical design.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded source-based drafting is plausible, without a documented policy-development case in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing health benefit, resources and practicable service rules.
tasks.human_edge: Own the clinical rationale and recognise implementation consequences.
tasks.altitude: Less initial wording; no new organisational decision rights.

reach.task: Assess practical effects of nutrition policies
reach.learn: Test proposed rules against care delivery

evidence.claim: A source-constrained policy drafting aid is plausible model knowledge; its time estimate and suitability are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary ends at a policy recommendation; adoption, staff training and service delivery are unchanged and outside this task.
Dietitian produces scope, goals, source versions and unresolved choices in s1 with capture fully retained. No machine-ready legal or clinical policy rules are assumed.
Try existing document templates first. Missing evidence returns the relevant section to manual development.
Four additional focal hours cover source updates and policy-template audits.
research_questions: Does referenced drafting save time after clinical and implementation review?

already_counted.description: Tradeoff assessment and final recommendation confirmation

approvals.approved_version: Exact policy recommendation, scope, clauses, source versions and unresolved decisions; edits require renewed confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+24+35=84, gross=16, upkeep=4, net=12. High assumes 40% less initial wording effort for familiar policy topics; low retains manual drafting for novel or conflicting evidence plus upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Physical monitoring and meal inspection stay intact; order entry and initial policy wording may take less time.
reach: Trace specification changes with dietetic technicians
Test nutrition policy practicality with registered nurses
role.ambitious_version: A dietitian with traceable purchase drafts and policy recommendations who retains direct nutritional and food safety judgement.
